title: Parallel shard handoff for low-latency telemetry ingress
creator: Samir Patel
description: Implement a parallelized shard-handoff path for Console telemetry ingest that reduces tail latency during load spikes and provides graceful spillover. The new sidecar/processor will consumer telemetry events from the edge gateway, route them into hot shards for low-latency routing, and perform spill-to-object-storage for overloaded shards. Goals: 1) maintain 99th-percentile ingest latency < 120ms under 5x baseline traffic, 2) avoid data loss during transient broker outages, 3) provide operational visibility and cost controls for spill events.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end ingest path with Redpanda-backed hot shards and S3 spillover deployed to staging
99th-percentile latency for telemetry ingest measured on staging under a 5x synthetic workload is < 120ms
Automatic spill-to-S3 triggers after configured queue depth and written manifest objects validated by downstream batch replayer
Dedup window implemented (Redis LRU cache + RocksDB local store) with false-positive rate < 0.01% for 24h window
Operational dashboards with per-shard backlog, spill rate, and replayer lag are published
Graceful degradation test documented and runbook updated
updates: 2026-02-15: Ticket created. Initial scope and performance goals set with PM. Assigned to Priya.

2026-02-18: Architecture sync — agreed to evaluate Redpanda (local Raft) for lower tail latency and simpler ops vs cloud-managed Kafka. Decided Redpanda compatibility mode for Kafka clients to minimize client changes.

2026-02-25: Prototype sidecar that accepts HTTP/Protobuf payloads and writes to in-memory hot shard queue completed (PR: github.com/redwood/telemetry/PR-1847). Measurements show median latency 20ms, p95 85ms at baseline.

2026-03-02: Backpressure strategy iterated — token-bucket per-shard + prioritized spill queue. Design doc updated to include spill manifest format and replayer contract (Confluence: /display/TELEMETRY/Shard+Handoff+Design).
2026-03-05: Security review kickoff. We must encrypt spill manifests and sign S3 objects for integrity; added KMS key use — security review required flag set.
2026-03-08: Integration test failing on replayer duplicate suppression during replays. Investigating dedup key collision; increased key namespace to include event origin and shard id as prefix.
2026-03-10: Load test in staging: 5x traffic shows p99 ingest latency 140ms with default config. Tuned batch flush thresholds and reduced p99 to 118ms. Preparing release candidate for console-2026.03
notes: Trade-offs considered: strict exactly-once via Kafka transactions was rejected due to increased tail latency and complexity for cross-region replication. We accept at-least-once with dedup as the pragmatic choice.

Operational model: hot shards handled by Redpanda for low-latency; cold/overloaded shards spill to S3 with manifest files that downstream replayers consume. Spill events are charged to customer token buckets to discourage excessive usage.

Dedup strategy: short-term in-memory Redis LRU for most recent keys (O(10M) entries), persistent RocksDB for longer retention across restarts. Dedup keys include event_id + origin + shard_prefix to avoid collisions.
Open questions: whether to use per-customer QoS shaping at ingress vs global shard-level QoS. PM prefers per-customer shaping but implementation complexity may push to a follow-up ticket.
Follow-ups: create a separate EPIC to add cross-region spill replication and faster replayer parallelism (post GA).
